name: AllTrails Plus
subcategory: trip planning, navigation and travel intelligence
tagline: Organize user-imported GPX routes and offline trip notes without copying trail data

tiers.name: Base
tiers.limits: Search and save from 500,000+ trails; record, review, and share activities; 0 offline map downloads

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Offline maps, wrong-turn alerts, trail conditions, Garmin integration, and no ads; 7-day trial
tiers.notes: $35.99 billed annually; the site displays the rounded equivalent as $2.99/month.

tiers.name: Peak
tiers.limits: Everything in Plus plus custom route creation/editing, heatmaps, Outdoor Lens, and backpacking tools; 7-day trial for eligible new users
tiers.notes: $79.99 billed annually; existing Plus subscribers are charged a new 12-month Peak term and receive platform-specific credit/refund treatment.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free Base plan: 500,000+ searchable trails and unlimited-looking save/record access with no published numeric save cap; 0 offline maps, 0 custom route editing, and 0 heatmaps.
pricing.billingTerms: annual only; no monthly plan; eligible subscriptions begin with a 7-day trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: A card is required for the trial and billing starts on day 7; prior trial users may be charged immediately. Plus-to-Peak upgrades can trigger a full new annual charge before the old-plan credit or refund is applied.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For AllTrails Plus, organize user-imported GPX routes and offline trip notes without copying trail data. The hard boundary is massive trail database, reviews, conditions, maps, community, and mobile navigation, plus proprietary live data and network coverage.
coreLoopDIY: Organize user-imported GPX routes and trip notes, map user-entered places and reservations, and keep an offline itinerary without copying proprietary trail data or claiming live availability.
requirements: optional public transit or weather API
whatYouLose: massive trail database, reviews, conditions, maps, community, and mobile navigation
booking, disruption support, and offline map fleet
moatNotes: proprietary live data and network coverage
ongoingBurden: map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for AllTrails Plus because travel subscriptions sell current data and confidence during disruption, not just an itinerary list. The recurring cost buys map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Wanderer
priorArt.desc: Open-source self-hosted trail database and route explorer using open map data.

alternatives.name: OsmAnd~
alternatives.desc: Offline topo maps, routes and GPX on Android; trail discovery is OpenStreetMap, not AllTrails.

alternatives.name: Organic Maps
alternatives.desc: Offline OSM maps, bookmarks and GPX files with no account and no subscription.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Wanderer
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A fine GPX route library, but it does not provide offline trip notes on the trail.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Plus plan and a personal itinerary organizer DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for AllTrails Plus in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, MapLibre GL, and user-supplied map and travel APIs; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize user-imported GPX routes and trip notes, map user-entered places and reservations, and keep an offline itinerary without copying proprietary trail data or claiming live availability.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create trips, days, places, reservations, notes, documents, packing items, and emergency contacts.
Geocode only user-entered places and display them through MapLibre with cached trip-area tiles where allowed.
Parse forwarded reservation text locally into editable fields without logging message content.
Build a day timeline, route overview, conflict warnings, timezone display, and offline printable itinerary.
Allow manual updates for delays and reservations and label all external data with source and timestamp.
Export a complete trip bundle as JSON, calendar file, Markdown, and PDF.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out live flight, hotel, award, or ticket inventory.
Deliberately leave out commercial turn-by-turn navigation and global offline maps.
Deliberately leave out booking guarantees, disruption rebooking, and traveler support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
